bugs.error_message: Corrupt .wolf/nudge-state.json silently destroyed every nudge disposition (dismissals, resolutions, snoozes, lineage counts) on the next write, with no diagnostic.
bugs.root_cause: readState() caught ENOENT and JSON parse errors in one branch and returned emptyState() for both. A corrupt-but-present file therefore looked identical to a first run, and the next writeStateOrThrow persisted the empty state over real data. The in-code comment claimed corruption was reported via writeStateOrThrow validation, but that function only validates the body it is about to write, never the bytes just read.
bugs.fix: Split absent from corrupt in readState: read bytes first (ENOENT -> empty state is correct), then parse. On a parse failure quarantine the original bytes to nudge-state.json.corrupt-<ts> and invoke an onCorrupt callback; engine.evaluate logs it as a state_corrupt diagnostic. Regression test 31.

bugs.error_message: max_emissions_per_rule_per_session could be breached by concurrent Stop hooks: 8 concurrent processes produced 8 emissions against a ceiling of 1.
bugs.root_cause: The per-rule session ceiling was filtered only on the state snapshot engine.evaluate reads before taking any lock. tryClaim re-read state inside the lock but checked only disposition, same-fingerprint emission, and lease -- never the per-rule count. Concurrent Stops holding DISTINCT fingerprints of the SAME rule each observed count 0, so every one of them claimed and emitted.
bugs.fix: Re-check the ceiling inside tryClaim against durable state, counting live leases as well as emissions so the window between a competitor claim and its markEmitted is covered; leases now carry rule_id. Engine passes ruleId/maxPerRulePerSession and routes an OVER_BUDGET refusal to queued rather than suppressed. Negative control: disabling the in-lock check yields 8 emissions vs 1. Regression test 30.

bugs.error_message: A pending review staged for file set {a} still reported CURRENT after the target set expanded to {a,b}, so the stale entry was never flagged and could later be completed with --reviewed-current as though it covered b.
bugs.root_cause: isSnapshotCurrent iterated only Object.keys(pending.content_hashes) and compared those against current bytes. A file present in currentHashes but absent from the recorded snapshot was invisible to the check, so coverage was asymmetric: drift was detected but scope EXPANSION was not.
bugs.fix: Added the reverse pass — every key in currentHashes must exist in the recorded snapshot, else the snapshot is superseded. Supersede reason now distinguishes drifted (changed) from added (entered scope) files so an empty drift list cannot render as a vague "target(s) changed", and evidence carries added_files. Regression test 34 with negative control (fails when the reverse pass is removed).

bugs.error_message: Incomplete fix for bug-471: when the corruption-quarantine write itself failed, readState still returned a plain empty state, so the next write overwrote the corrupt bytes and permanently destroyed every disposition anyway.
bugs.root_cause: The bug-471 fix reported corruption honestly (onCorrupt fired with quarantine:null) but returned an ordinary empty state. Nothing downstream distinguished "empty because absent" from "empty because unrecoverable", so writeStateOrThrow renamed over the only surviving copy of the data. The path had been probed, but only for whether the failure was REPORTED — not for whether the data SURVIVED.
bugs.fix: readState marks the fallback with a non-enumerable UNSAFE_TO_PERSIST symbol when quarantine fails; writeStateOrThrow throws on that marker, routing callers through the existing degraded path so tryClaim returns {ok:false, degraded:true} and the corrupt bytes stay intact. Symbol-keyed and non-enumerable so it never reaches JSON.stringify or a fingerprint. Verified all 6 mutators (tryClaim, markEmitted, releaseLease, setDisposition, bumpLineageRound, markLineageEscalated) preserve the corrupt bytes. Regression test 35 with an injected>0 precondition and a negative control.

bugs.error_message: OpenWolf review completion failed: could not lock /mnt/j/projectshome/projects/customopenwolf/.wolf/reviewlog.json — hit 4 times in one session, each with a recorded owner pid that was already dead.
bugs.root_cause: acquireFileLock records the owner pid and isLockReclaimable already knows how to check liveness via isProcessAlive — but that check was gated behind `age > staleMs` (30s). The acquire timeout is only 2s. So when a Stop hook crashed while holding the lock, its lock was "fresh" by mtime for 30 seconds and therefore never reclaimable, while every caller inside that window failed hard after burning the full 2s timeout. Freshness by mtime was being treated as evidence the lock is still HELD, which it is not.
bugs.fix: Check owner liveness BEFORE the mtime gate: inside the `age <= staleMs` branch, if the lock is older than a 250ms grace period and its recorded pid is dead, reclaim immediately. A dead pid is definitive evidence. The grace period avoids racing a lock written microseconds ago. Same-pid locks stay protected because isProcessAlive(process.pid) is true, preserving the existing in-process-holder contract. Measured: dead owner 2001ms hard failure -> 2ms reclaim; live owner still correctly refused (not stolen). Synced to all 4 copies (src .ts/.js, .wolf/utils, templates/wolf/utils). Regression test 36 with negative control.

bugs.error_message: Self-introduced regression: adding process.on('uncaughtException') to the Stop hook SWALLOWED uncaught exceptions — the process kept running and exited 0 instead of terminating with code 1.
bugs.root_cause: Node's default behavior for an uncaught exception is to print the stack and terminate with exit code 1. Registering ANY 'uncaughtException' listener replaces that default — the process continues running after the handler returns. I added the listener purely for diagnostics (hook lifecycle instrumentation) without realizing it changes control flow. For a Claude Code Stop hook this is serious: Claude Code parses the hook's stdout as a JSON contract, so a hook that continues in a corrupted state after an uncaught exception can emit output that is parsed as a valid result. Same hazard for 'unhandledRejection'. This is the exact failure class the instrumentation was meant to diagnose — a diagnostic that silently changes behavior.
bugs.fix: Restore the default disposition inside each handler: log the event, then process.exit(1). Measured before: a bare listener printed 'STILL RUNNING after throw' and exited 0. After: handler logs and exits 1, matching Node's no-listener baseline (also measured as exit 1). Verified that main().catch(() => exitWithStopHookResult(false)) is NOT preempted — an attached .catch() means the rejection is handled, so 'unhandledRejection' never fires and the graceful path is preserved. Synced to all 4 layers (src .ts/.js, .wolf/hooks, templates/wolf/hooks) preserving each layer's differing sourcemap-footer convention.

bugs.error_message: Buglog multi-edit nudge fired on prose: editing a .md/.csv/.txt three times triggered 'files edited 3+ times ... log any bugs fixed.' Reported by an external AI review after hitting it three times in one session.
bugs.root_cause: checkForMissingBugLogs filtered candidates ONLY through buglog_scan_excludes (22 path globs covering scratch/test/.wolf docs) and never checked file type. The multi-edit obligation is a code concept — 'you edited it 3x to get it right, that's probably a bug' — but three edits to a prose document is authoring. bugs.error_message: False-positive acknowledgement of the buglog nudge did not persist: the same file and the same non-bug re-nudged on the next edit. Only the per-session cap bounded the loop.
bugs.root_cause: The ack signature payload was [normalizedPath, count, latestEditMs]. Including the count AND the timestamp meant an ack expired immediately: acking at 3 edits didn't cover 4, and because the timestamp also moved it didn't even cover a 4th evaluation at an UNCHANGED count. Measured: ack@3/t=1000 -> 292aca150216; 4 edits -> MISS; same count later edit -> MISS.
bugs.fix: Signature is now the normalized FILE SET only. What the user asserts by acking is a claim about the file ('repeatedly editing this isn't a bug fix'); that claim doesn't expire because they edited it again. Scope stays bounded — acks live in _session.json (one session) and a genuinely NEW file in the multi-edit set changes the set and correctly re-nudges. Verified both directions; the pre-existing test that asserted re-fire at 4 edits encoded the defect and was updated with a negative control.

bugs.error_message: Review nudge reported '~297 new lines since last review (threshold 40)' for changes nowhere near that size, including on Markdown-only edits.
bugs.root_cause: effectiveLines = (cumulativeTokens - coveredTokens)/17 where cumulativeTokens was sessionEntry.totals.output_tokens_estimated — the WHOLE session's output, including reasoning, tool results, and writes to files the review scope explicitly excludes. A one-line edit to an in-scope file inherited the entire session's volume. At min_diff_lines 40 (~680 tokens) that fires on essentially any edit late in a working session. NOTE: the external report framed this as 'prose lines counted as code lines'; the actual mechanism is token attribution, not line counting — a materially different bug with a different fix.
bugs.fix: Attribute tokens to the in-scope writes themselves (sum w.tokens for writes whose normalized path survived scope_excludes), falling back to the session total only when no write carries a tokens field so older _session.json degrades to previous behavior rather than reporting 0 and silently disabling the gate. Measured: a 51000-token session with one 85-token in-scope edit reported 3000 lines before, 5 lines after; a genuinely large 3400-token in-scope change still fires (200 lines). Added covered_tokens_basis so units are self-describing — a pre-change baseline in session-total units would otherwise clamp the delta to 0 and permanently disable the size trigger for that session.

bugs.error_message: Duplicate 'edited N times this session' nudge in post-write.ts fired on every file type with no excludes and no per-session cap. Not present in the external report — found while verifying it.
bugs.root_cause: post-write.ts:279 emitted the same multi-edit buglog reminder to stderr gated ONLY by isWolfAllowlisted. It had no extension filter, no buglog_scan_excludes, and no firing cap — so it fired on every .md/.csv/.txt edited 3+ times, and would have kept firing even after the Stop-hook site was fixed.
bugs.fix: Routed through the same carriesBugfixObligation predicate the Stop hook uses, with the same excludes and project-derived extension set. The predicate lives in shared.js precisely so 'does this file carry an obligation' has ONE definition rather than four divergent ones; globToRegex moved to shared.js for the same reason (two glob implementations = two places for the `noauth` substring bug to return).

bugs.error_message: Review size trigger could compute 0 lines and silently not fire, despite real in-scope work. Self-found while reviewing my own bug-498 fix; no user report.
bugs.root_cause: The scoped-attribution fix set its sawTokenField flag from ANY write carrying a tokens field -- including writes excluded by review scope_excludes -- while scopedTokens only summed IN-SCOPE writes. A _session.json spanning the upgrade, whose only in-scope write predates per-write token recording but which also contains an excluded write that has the field, took the scoped path and summed 0. Measured: sawTokenField true, scoped 0, effectiveLines 0, gate does not fire. The guard and the value it guarded were computed over different populations.
bugs.fix: Decide per-scope and require attribution to be COMPLETE: count in-scope writes, and only trust the sum when every in-scope write carries a finite tokens field; otherwise fall back to sessionEntry.totals.output_tokens_estimated. Partial data now over-reports (visible) instead of under-reporting (silent). The four covered_tokens_basis stamp sites were repointed to the same attributionComplete condition -- stamping the scoped marker while storing a session-total value would write a mislabeled baseline, reintroducing the unit-mixing bug one layer down. Regression test added with 4 negative controls (small in-scope edit still 5 lines not 3000; large still fires; partial falls back; no-tokens falls back).

bugs.error_message: Review size trigger silently skipped when every in-scope write was a pure deletion (tokens: 0). Found by minimax companion review of review-0077.
bugs.root_cause: attributionComplete trusted any sum whose in-scope writes all carried a valid finite token field -- including a sum of ZERO. estimateTokens measures 'content || new_string' with Math.ceil, so any non-empty content yields >=1, BUT an Edit that deletes a block has an empty new_string and records tokens: 0. Verified reachable: Write with empty content -> 0, Edit deleting a block -> 0, normal Edit -> 4. A session whose in-scope writes are all deletions therefore computed attributionComplete=true over a 0-token sum -> effectiveLines 0 -> size trigger never fired. Deleting 500 lines is precisely the change that most needs review.
bugs.fix: Added a 'scopedTokens > 0' clause to attributionComplete so a zero total falls back to the session total. NOTE the reviewer's suggested fix was wrong and was NOT applied: it proposed rejecting tokens: 0 in the per-write validity predicate, which misclassifies a legitimate measurement as malformed and breaks the mixed case (a deletion alongside a real edit would wrongly fall back to session totals). Guard the SUM, not the individual value. Falsifier: single deletion tokens=0 -> 294 lines, fires (independently matches the value the reviewer predicted in its falsifier); control -- mixed deletion + real edit -> 6 lines, does NOT fall back to the 51000-token session total. Also hardened the validity predicate to reject negatives and extracted it to one hasUsableTokens definition, since two copies of that predicate caused the round-2 population mismatch.

bugs.error_message: Scoped review attribution (bug-498) never executed in production: attributionComplete was false on 100% of runs. Found independently by chatgpt AND kimi companion review of review-0077.
bugs.root_cause: Field-name mismatch between the sole producer and the consumer. sessionEntry.writes is built at stop.ts:711-714 as {file, tokens_estimated, action} -- the persisted ledger schema -- but maybeNudgeReview's hasUsableTokens tested `typeof w.tokens === 'number'`, which is undefined on every element. So sawTokenField was always false, attributionComplete always false, and cumulativeTokens always took the session-total fallback that INCLUDES scope-excluded writes -- the exact mis-attribution bug-498 existed to remove. bug-501 and bug-504, built on top, were likewise dead. Verified by executing the real producer mapper: writes [{tokens_estimated:0},{tokens_estimated:100}] + excluded 10000 -> attributionComplete false, 594 lines instead of the intended 6.
bugs.fix: Added writeTokens(w) reading tokens_estimated with a `tokens` fallback (so a caller passing the raw files_written shape still attributes rather than silently falling back), and routed hasUsableTokens and the accumulator through it. Fixing the producer instead was rejected: tokens_estimated is the persisted ledger schema and renaming it would break every historical _session.json.

bugs.error_message: Unit test suite passed 103/103 against a feature that never ran once in production.
bugs.root_cause: The attribution test defined its own decide() helper that REIMPLEMENTED the rule using w.tokens -- mirroring the author's mental model, so it agreed with that model's bug. A test that re-declares the logic it tests can only ever confirm its author; it has no independent access to the truth.
bugs.fix: Two defenses. (1) decide() now builds writes through the SAME mapper shape the hook uses, so a producer/consumer divergence changes the fixture too. (2) A structural test reads the shipped src/hooks/stop.ts, extracts the producer's emitted field name by regex, and asserts the consumer accessor reads that field. Verified the structural test genuinely FAILS on the defect: reintroducing `const writeTokens = (w) => w.tokens` yields `not ok 8 ... attribution reads a different field than the producer emits (producer: "tokens_estimated")`. A test that passes on both broken and fixed code is worse than no test.

bugs.error_message: covered_tokens and covered_tokens_basis could disagree, subtracting baselines across incommensurable token scales and silently killing the review size trigger. Found by chatgpt arbitration (direction 1) and self-check (direction 2).
bugs.root_cause: Value and marker were written as two independent statements: `covered_tokens = Math.max(stored, cumulative)` unconditionally, then `if (attributionComplete) basis = SCOPED`. Both directions break: (1) a stored SCOPED marker survives a fallback turn, leaving a session-TOTAL value labeled scoped; (2) Math.max retains an older larger session-total value while the current scoped turn stamps SCOPED over it. Either way a later scoped turn subtracts a session-scale baseline from scoped tokens -> clamp to 0 lines -> gate dead on real work. The read side had the same flaw independently: it picked the numerically largest baseline ACROSS bases, so a session-total entry out-ranked a scoped one purely because its scale is larger, then donated its basis.
bugs.fix: Added advanceCoveredTokens(entry, cumulative, complete): same basis -> Math.max (meaningful); different or absent basis -> adopt the current turn's value outright, because comparing across scales is meaningless. The marker always describes the value ACTUALLY RETAINED. Session-total baselines are now stamped explicitly (TOKEN_BASIS_SESSION) instead of left unmarked, so 'old scheme' and 'this turn fell back' are distinguishable. Read-side selection is now basis-matched first and magnitude second, with the post-hoc zeroing kept as a backstop.

bugs.error_message: One shared obligation predicate returned OPPOSITE answers in the two hooks for the same file. Found by kimi companion review of review-0077 (rated LOW).
bugs.root_cause: carriesBugfixObligation tested a single path form, but its two callers naturally hold different ones: post-write.ts passes the absolute path while stop.ts iterates edit_counts keys, which post-write stores as project-RELATIVE for in-project files. Excludes are ^...$-anchored globs matching one form only, so for a project checked out under /tmp the default `/tmp/**` exclude suppressed the post-write nudge while the Stop hook still fired; symmetrically a root-anchored exclude like `src/scratch/**` matched only the relative key. This broke the 'one predicate, same semantics in both hooks' contract asserted in that code's own comment. A stale comment in stop.ts also claimed edit_counts keys are absolute.
bugs.fix: carriesBugfixObligation now accepts opts.altPaths and excludes if ANY supplied form matches -- an exclude states the file is uninteresting, and which spelling the caller holds should not change that. post-write passes the relative editKey alongside the absolute path; stop.ts resolves relative keys against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and passes the absolute form. Stale comment corrected. Verified on shipped bytes: project under /tmp, file src/a.sh -> both hooks suppressed, AGREE: yes. Negative control: a file matching neither exclude still nudges in both forms.

bugs.error_message: Two end-to-end stop-hook tests began failing after the attribution field fix (expected ~59 new lines, got ~118).
bugs.root_cause: Not a regression -- a dead safety rule waking up. The fixtures wrote an UNMARKED legacy baseline (covered_tokens with no covered_tokens_basis). With attribution finally live, the bug-498 unit-safety rule correctly refuses to subtract a session-total baseline from scoped tokens. That rule had been unreachable the entire time attribution was inert, because both sides were using session totals. Refusing is correct: a legacy covered_tokens sums ALL writes including scope-excluded ones, so session_total >= scoped_sum always; the hook cannot tell a safe legacy entry (no excluded writes, bases coincide) from an unsafe one (a 40000-token excluded scratch write -> clamp to 0 -> gate dead), because legacy entries do not record their basis. Refusing over-nudges visibly; honoring risks silent death.
bugs.fix: Updated both fixtures to carry covered_tokens_basis: 'scoped-writes' (the shape all new entries have) and to assert the new entry records its own basis. Added a third test pinning the legacy-refusal behavior explicitly (unmarked baseline -> 118 lines, not 59) so it cannot regress unnoticed. The fixture helper takes an optional coveredBasis and omits the field when absent, reproducing a genuine pre-bug-498 entry.

bugs.error_message: npm run build was invoked from the driving skillsbench directory and failed with ENOENT because that directory has no package.json.
bugs.root_cause: The Bash tool retains the session working directory; the first build command omitted --prefix or an explicit customopenwolf working directory.
bugs.fix: Re-ran the build with npm --prefix /mnt/j/projectshome/projects/customopenwolf run build, then used explicit absolute paths or cd for all remaining verification commands.

bugs.error_message: Skill receipts over absent tombstone inputs or empty manifests could validate and verify CURRENT with strong attestation.
bugs.root_cause: Strong attestation validation treated stable absence as valid byte identity and did not require any input artifacts.
bugs.fix: Require at least one input for non-snapshot receipts, reject tombstone/unreadable inputs for manifest-bound or externally-verifiable attestations, and return MALFORMED for non-snapshot tombstone verification.

bugs.error_message: makeArtifactManifest silently dropped declared files that lacked hash entries, allowing invisible receipt scope shrinkage.
bugs.root_cause: The shared makeHashManifest compatibility helper filters files without hashes; the new generic builder inherited that permissive behavior.
bugs.fix: Make the generic builder fail closed when any normalized declared artifact lacks a hash while preserving review helper compatibility.

bugs.error_message: Skill receipt validation accepted malformed evidence entries and invalid or inverted timestamps.
bugs.root_cause: The v1 validator checked only evidence array-ness and timestamp string types, not element shape, parseability, or ordering.
bugs.fix: Validate non-empty evidence kind/value strings, require parseable receipt/invocation timestamps, and reject finished_at earlier than started_at.

bugs.error_message: Fresh openwolf init copied ESM utility JavaScript into .wolf/utils without a local package.json declaring type=module.
bugs.root_cause: The init hook installer wrote .wolf/hooks/package.json but omitted the matching module boundary for sibling .wolf/utils; update.ts already had the required manifest and existing tests masked the fresh-init difference.
bugs.fix: Write .wolf/utils/package.json with type=module during fresh init and exercise an actual fresh hook import in tests/skill-deployment.test.js.

bugs.error_message: wolfpack qa status --check exited 1 with 71 stale, 4 orphaned, and 12 broken historical reductions.
bugs.root_cause: The repository contains long-standing historical QA reductions whose target bytes or required frontmatter no longer match; the release-specific reductions are current but --check reports aggregate repository state.
bugs.fix: Verified the release-specific managed-skill, fresh-init-utils, and skill-receipt reductions separately as CURRENT; retained historical drift for a dedicated cleanup rather than rewriting unrelated evidence during this release.

bugs.error_message: External review found same-minute backup directory collisions and reviewlog.json omission from update backups.
bugs.root_cause: Backup names used minute-granular timestamps without collision handling, and USER_DATA_FILES omitted reviewlog.json despite init treating it as durable user data.
bugs.fix: Added collision-safe numeric suffixes, included reviewlog.json in backups, and added a two-update regression test that verifies distinct backups and preserved review history.

bugs.error_message: External review found restore could delete user edits to a managed skill when that file was absent at backup time.
bugs.root_cause: The absence marker was interpreted as authority to unlink the current managed path even though bytes created or edited after update were not present in the backup.
bugs.fix: Restore now reinstates backed-up prior bytes; when the path was previously absent, it removes the current file only if those bytes still exactly match the trusted packaged template, preserving divergent post-update user edits. Regression coverage verifies unchanged introduced managed bytes are removed.

bugs.error_message: External review found the cron quoting regression test was vacuous against alternate shell-quoting regressions.
bugs.root_cause: The initial test used shell syntax validation, then execution with only apostrophes; those inputs did not distinguish canonical single-quote escaping from double quoting that permits shell expansion.
bugs.fix: Changed the test to execute the generated command with apostrophes, $HOME, $USER, and $(id -u) in paths and assert exact literal argv captured in the redirected log.

bugs.error_message: Initial K-Dense scientific manager fixture build failed after mechanical source substitution and five scientific tests initially failed.
bugs.root_cause: A hyphenated metadata property was generated as an invalid bare TypeScript key, and copied fixture paths/expectations still referenced SkillsBench state, pdf, six skills, and the shorter cron argv.
bugs.fix: Replaced the metadata key with scientificSkillsCommit, corrected all scientific fixture paths and IDs, updated the nine-skill count and exact scientific cron argv, then rebuilt and passed all 15 focused manager/deployment tests.

bugs.error_message: Final arbitration found rollback lock metadata stayed on the newer release and cron entries did not escape percent characters.
bugs.root_cause: Release directories had no persisted commit/skill manifest for rollback lock reconstruction, and shell quoting was incorrectly assumed sufficient for crontab's special percent parsing.
bugs.fix: Persisted release.json metadata, restored commit and skill hashes during rollback before doctor verification, escaped percent only when rendering crontab lines, and strengthened both manager tests with post-rollback doctor and percent fixtures.
